title: Kindred
summary: The vampires' own name for themselves: the undead children of Caine who feed on mortal blood.

claims.text: Vampires make their homes in cities and see everything beyond them as dangerous ground, held by Lupines and worse.
To Kindred, cities are patchworks of territories and domains, almost medieval in outlook.

title: The Embrace
summary: How a mortal is made a vampire: drained of blood, then given a little of the sire's.

claims.text: To Embrace, a vampire drains the victim and then gives back a small amount of the vampire's own blood.
The new vampire is the sire's childe; a newly made one still under the sire's protection is a fledgling.

title: Generation
summary: How many steps of the Embrace separate a vampire from Caine, and so how potent the vampire's blood is.

claims.text: Each Embrace makes the childe one Generation further from Caine than the sire.
The Clan founders are of the Third Generation, and the Thirteenth is common in modern nights.
Generation sets how much blood a vampire can hold and how far certain Disciplines can be mastered.
Vampires of the Fifteenth Generation cannot sire at all, and the rise of the thin-blooded is read as a sign of the End Times.

title: Diablerie
summary: Drinking another vampire's blood and soul to Final Death, the way to lower one's Generation.

claims.text: Diablerie consumes a vampire's blood until the victim meets Final Death, and can permanently lower the diablerist's Generation.
Elders call it the Amaranth.
Once the blood is gone, the diablerist makes an extended Strength roll at difficulty 9 to take the victim's essence, each success an unsoakable aggravated health level.
For a month for each Generation of difference, sensitive Kindred feel something wrong about a diablerist.

title: Caine
summary: The First Vampire of Kindred legend, the source of every vampire's curse.

claims.text: The Camarilla mostly treats the tale of Caine as a symbolic parable; the Sabbat takes it literally.
Belief in Caine is a religion among vampires, with all the zeal and intolerance of any faith.

title: The Book of Nod
summary: The scattered scripture of the Kindred, telling of Caine, the First City and the end of days.

claims.text: Many of the doomsday prophecies Kindred fear come from this scripture.
It teaches that the coming of the thin-blooded is a sign that Gehenna is near.

title: Antediluvians
summary: The Third Generation, founders of the thirteen Clans, said to sleep until Gehenna.

claims.text: Antediluvian means one of the Third Generation, the eldest Kindred in existence.
The Clans were reputedly founded by the Third Generation.
At Gehenna they are expected to wake and devour their descendants.

title: Gehenna
summary: The prophesied end of the Kindred, when the Antediluvians rise and the race of Caine is destroyed.

claims.text: In the legends the sky rains blood, the Antediluvians wake and feed on their childer, and Caine returns to judge.
Most Kindred fear it whether or not they believe in it.

title: Golconda
summary: A fabled state of transcendence in which a vampire masters the Beast.

claims.text: Golconda is a near-mythical state of true mastery over the Beast.
The Inconnu are a loose confederation of Kindred who seek it.

title: The Jyhad
summary: The endless secret war of the elders, fought through younger Kindred and mortal pawns.

claims.text: The Jyhad is the spiteful, age-old war of schemes the elders wage on one another.
Elders, vampires of two centuries or more, are its keenest players.

title: The Masquerade
summary: The First Tradition: hiding the existence of vampires from mortals.

claims.text: The First Tradition forbids revealing a vampire's nature to anyone not of the Blood, on pain of losing all claims of the Blood.

title: The Traditions
summary: The six ancient laws of the Kindred that the Camarilla upholds.

claims.text: The six Traditions are the Masquerade, the Domain, the Progeny, the Accounting, Hospitality and Destruction.
The Traditions sit at the heart of Camarilla practice.

title: The Progeny and the Accounting
summary: The Traditions that govern making new vampires: permission first, and a sire answers for the childe.

claims.text: A vampire may Embrace only with an elder's leave; an unsanctioned sire and childe may both be destroyed.
Until released, a childe must obey the sire, and the sire bears the childe's sins.

title: Destruction and the Blood Hunt
summary: The Tradition that forbids killing another vampire and reserves the Blood Hunt to the eldest.

claims.text: Only the eldest may destroy a vampire or call a Blood Hunt.

title: Prince
summary: The Camarilla ruler of a city, who claims it as a domain under the Traditions.

claims.text: Princes claim whole cities as domains and may let lesser vampires hold territory within them.
By the Fifth Tradition a visiting vampire must present to the ruler of the city.

title: Elysium
summary: Neutral ground where vampires meet without violence, usually in places of culture.

claims.text: Elysium is a gathering place where vampires may meet without fear of harm, often an opera house, theatre or museum.
The Sabbat respects it less than the Camarilla does.

title: Ghouls
summary: Mortals fed vampire blood without being drained, made into servants.

claims.text: A ghoul is made by feeding a mortal a little vitae without first draining the mortal's blood.
A ghoul's master is called the domitor.

title: The Blood Bond
summary: The enslaving love that comes from drinking the same vampire's blood on three nights.

claims.text: Drinking one vampire's blood on three occasions creates a blood bond, and taking a vampire's blood acknowledges that vampire's mastery.
Vinculi made through the Vaulderie do not fade over time as ordinary blood bonds do.

title: The Vaulderie
summary: The Sabbat rite of shared blood that replaces the blood bond with loyalty to the pack.

claims.text: Pack members who skip the Vaulderie for more than a month are shunned at best and destroyed at worst.
The bond it creates is the Vinculum, rated by a die roll the first time a character takes part.
Six points of Vaulderie vitae wear down an existing blood bond and replace it with Vinculi.

title: Sects
summary: The great factions of the Kindred: the Anarch Movement, the Camarilla and the Sabbat, with others beside.

claims.text: Of all the Sects, three are best known: the Anarch Movement, the Camarilla and the Sabbat.
Kindred who belong to no Sect and refuse a Prince's claim are Autarkis, often lone outcasts.

title: The Camarilla
summary: The largest Sect, which upholds the Traditions and the Masquerade under elders and Princes.

claims.text: Its traditional strongholds are Chicago, New Orleans, Vienna, London and Paris.
The Traditions are at the heart of the Sect.
Brujah call it the Ivory Tower.

title: The Sabbat
summary: The Sect opposed to the Camarilla, which rejects humanity and wages war on the Antediluvians.

claims.text: Its traditional strongholds are Detroit, Miami, Mexico City, Montreal and Madrid.
The Code of Milan sets out the Sect's laws.
The Lasombra and Tzimisce stand apart in it; most other Sabbat vampires reject Clan loyalty.

title: The Anarch Movement
summary: A movement of young vampires who reject the rule of elders.

claims.text: Its traditional strongholds are Los Angeles, San Diego and San Francisco.
The spirit of the old Anarch Revolt is flaring up again in the modern nights.

title: The Anarch Revolt
summary: The rising of young Kindred against their elders, centuries ago, that gave birth to the Camarilla and the Sabbat.

claims.text: The revolt of centuries past is the model for today's anarch unrest.

title: The Independent Clans
summary: Clans that stand outside the great Sects: the Assamites, Followers of Set, Giovanni and Ravnos.

claims.text: Their strongholds are Alamut for the Assamites, Cairo for the Followers of Set and Venice for the Giovanni.
Independent Clans often act like small Sects with agendas of their own.

title: The Inconnu
summary: A secretive confederation of elders seeking Golconda, who watch the other Sects.

claims.text: The Inconnu seek Golconda and rarely have more than one or two members in a domain.
A watcher, called a Monitor, may live in another Sect's domain to observe it.
Some think them a cult of would-be gods, others remnants of an old Roman conspiracy.

title: The Tal'Mahe'Ra
summary: The True Black Hand: a paranoid Sect based in the Underworld.

claims.text: Its stronghold lies in the Underworld, and it breeds ghouls on scattered estates.
Many Kindred doubt it exists at all.

title: Clans
summary: The thirteen great lineages of the Kindred, each passing on its Disciplines and its curse through the blood.

claims.text: There are thirteen known Clans, each reputedly founded by one of the Third Generation.
A Clan's members share traits passed down through the blood.
Vampires with no Clan are called Caitiff.

title: The Assamites
summary: The childer of Haqim, a Clan of assassins and judges based at Alamut.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Celerity, Obfuscate and Quietus.
Other Kindred call the childer of Haqim Assamites, and fear them as killers in the dark.
An Assamite's skin darkens with age, where other vampires grow paler.
Drinking another vampire's blood wounds an Assamite, a lethal level per point, because of a Tremere blood curse.

title: Clan Brujah
summary: Rebels and firebrands whose legacy of greatness is marred by their tempers.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Celerity, Potence and Presence.
Brujah history is one of past glory spoiled by the Clan's own fiery nature.
A Brujah has +2 difficulty to resist or steer a frenzy.

title: The Followers of Set
summary: Corrupters who peddle vice and serve their dark god from Cairo.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Obfuscate, Presence and Serpentis.
Setites trade in addiction, debasement and corruption, which many Kindred fear.
Sunlight does two extra health levels to a Setite, and bright light costs a die on actions.

title: Clan Gangrel
summary: Wild, bestial wanderers who make their havens in the wilderness.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Animalism, Fortitude and Protean.
Gangrel are predators of the wild places, and their havens often lack modern comforts.
Each frenzy leaves a Gangrel with a temporary animal trait.

title: Clan Giovanni
summary: A family Clan of necromancers who rose in Renaissance Venice.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Dominate, Necromancy and Potence.
The Giovanni family grew rich and powerful during the Venetian Renaissance.
They keep villas and estates as havens.
A Giovanni's Kiss brings mortals agony instead of pleasure, and can kill from shock.

title: Clan Lasombra
summary: Proud masters of shadow who lead the Sabbat.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Dominate, Obtenebration and Potence.
Lasombra would rather rule in hell than serve in heaven, and they lead through fear.
A Lasombra casts no reflection in mirror, water or glass.

title: Clan Malkavian
summary: Seers and madmen, cursed twice: by vampirism and by insanity.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Auspex, Dementation and Obfuscate.
Every Malkavian suffers the curse of the Kindred and a mind in turmoil as well.
Every Malkavian has one derangement that can never be cured, though Willpower can hold it off for a scene.

title: Clan Nosferatu
summary: Hideous information brokers who hide in sewers and warrens.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Animalism, Obfuscate and Potence.
The Embrace twists every Nosferatu into a monstrous form.
They often build warrens in sewers or tunnels.
A Nosferatu's Appearance is zero and can never be raised.

title: Clan Ravnos
summary: Wandering tricksters and thieves who move like rumours.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Animalism, Chimerstry and Fortitude.
The Ravnos are thieves and tricksters who rarely settle.
Each Ravnos has a vice, such as lying, cruelty or theft, that must be indulged when the chance comes unless resisted.

title: Clan Toreador
summary: Artists and aesthetes who see the night as a world of wonder.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Auspex, Celerity and Presence.
To the Toreador, nightfall reveals an endless realm of beauty.
When something truly remarkable is before a Toreador, a Self-Control or Instincts roll at difficulty 6 is needed to avoid being held spellbound.

title: Clan Tremere
summary: Blood sorcerers who were once something other than vampires.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Auspex, Dominate and Thaumaturgy.
The Tremere existed long ago as something other than vampires.
Many Tremere rely on the Clan's central chantry in a city.
A Tremere becomes blood bound after only two drinks of another vampire's blood instead of three.

title: Clan Tzimisce
summary: Old Eastern lords of flesh-shaping who stand with the Sabbat.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Animalism, Auspex and Vicissitude.
Members of the clan tend to keep one haven in common with the rest of their pack.
Each Tzimisce sleeps beside at least two fistfuls of soil taken from somewhere that mattered before the Embrace.

title: Clan Ventrue
summary: Lords and kings who claim the right to rule Kindred society.

claims.text: Its Disciplines are Dominate, Fortitude and Presence.
Through history the Ventrue have stood as leaders while other Clans schemed.
A Ventrue's haven reflects the vampire's dignity and must be kept flawless.
A Ventrue can feed on only one particular kind of mortal, chosen when the character is made.

title: Caitiff
summary: Vampires with no Clan, scorned by Kindred society.

claims.text: A Caitiff is a vampire of no Clan or none that is known, usually of high Generation, where the blood is too thin to pass on Clan traits.

title: Antitribu
summary: Members of a Clan who have turned against their Clan's Sect, usually by joining the Sabbat.

claims.text: Antitribu means anti-Clan; some have grown into bloodlines of their own.

title: Bloodlines
summary: Smaller lineages outside the thirteen Clans, such as the Baali, the Daughters of Cacophony and the Gargoyles.

claims.text: Legend says the Baali began with the childe of an Antediluvian who made a pact with dark powers to war on the Clans.
Song is the centre of every Daughter of Cacophony's existence.
The Tremere revealed the Gargoyle bloodline in 1167.

title: Coterie and Pack
summary: A small group of Kindred bound by need or interest; in the Sabbat, a pack.

claims.text: A coterie is a small band of Kindred; the Sabbat calls it a pack.

title: Neonates, Ancillae and Elders
summary: The ranks of age among vampires, from the newly made to those of centuries.

claims.text: An elder has two centuries or more of unlife; an ancilla is proven, between elders and neonates.

title: The Beast
summary: The predatory hunger and rage in every vampire, always testing the mind's control.

claims.text: The struggle between morality and monstrosity is the heart of the game.
As Humanity falls the Beast grows more prominent, and low-Humanity vampires may act on urges against their will.

title: Humanity
summary: The trait that measures how much of a vampire's mortal decency is left.

claims.text: Characters of Humanity 4 or less may be driven by urges that must be resisted with Conscience rolls.
Losing Humanity follows a hierarchy of sins and a degeneration roll.

title: Degeneration
summary: How a vampire loses Humanity or Path rating by committing sins against it.

claims.text: Sooner or later every vampire commits an atrocity, often in frenzy, and risks losing moral ground.

title: Virtues
summary: Conscience, Self-Control and Courage: the traits that hold the Beast in check.

claims.text: The three Virtues are Conscience, Self-Control and Courage.
Every character has Courage, whatever Path the character follows.

title: Willpower
summary: A vampire's drive and self-control, spent for automatic successes and to resist impulses.

claims.text: Willpower is a character's inner drive, the strength to overcome bad odds.

title: Frenzy
summary: When the Beast takes over in rage, hunger or terror.

claims.text: The Storyteller may call for a frenzy roll whenever a character could lose control.
Camarilla vampires couch threats in double talk to avoid setting off frenzy in public.
A vampire in frenzy gains temporary benefits from the state.

title: Paths of Enlightenment
summary: Moral codes some vampires follow instead of Humanity, each with its own sins.

claims.text: The Paths include Caine, Cathari, Death and the Soul, the Feral Heart, Harmony, Honorable Accord, Lilith, Metamorphosis, Night, Paradox, Power and the Inner Voice, and Typhon.
Following a Path takes discipline and spiritual strength of an inhuman kind; not just anyone can do it.

title: Aggravated Damage
summary: Wounds from fire, sunlight, claws and fangs that vampires heal only slowly.

claims.text: Vampires shrug off most bashing damage that would hurt a mortal badly.

title: Sunlight and Fire
summary: The two great banes of vampires, both causing aggravated damage.

claims.text: Even sunlight through a heavy curtain burns, and direct sun turns all but the mightiest vampires to ash; only Fortitude lets a vampire soak it.

title: Torpor
summary: Deathlike sleep that takes vampires who are badly hurt or very old.

claims.text: A vampire in torpor lies in a deathlike trance and can do nothing, not even spend blood, until enough time has passed.

title: Drugs in the Blood
summary: Vampires who feed on intoxicated mortals feel the drug themselves.

claims.text: Heroin, morphine and barbiturates in a victim's blood lower a vampire's Dexterity and Ability pools and make frenzy easier to resist.
Marijuana slows a vampire's sense of time and costs a die from Perception pools.

title: Disciplines
summary: The supernatural powers of the blood, from Animalism to Vicissitude.

claims.text: The Disciplines are Animalism, Auspex, Celerity, Chimerstry, Dementation, Dominate, Fortitude, Necromancy, Obfuscate, Obtenebration, Potence, Presence, Protean, Quietus, Serpentis, Thaumaturgy and Vicissitude.
Generation limits how far a vampire can master certain Disciplines.

title: Animalism
summary: Command and kinship with beasts, and in time the Beast itself.

claims.text: Animalism draws on the Beast in all creatures, from rats to elders, and amplifies the vampire's primal nature.

title: Auspex
summary: Heightened senses, auras and reading minds.

claims.text: Auspex heightens the senses and, with power, reveals auras and reads thoughts.

title: Celerity
summary: Supernatural speed.

claims.text: Celerity lets Assamites, Brujah and Toreador move so fast they blur.

title: Chimerstry
summary: The Ravnos art of illusion.

claims.text: The Ravnos are masters of illusion, though how they came by it is lost.

title: Dementation
summary: The Malkavian power to spread madness.

claims.text: Dementation channels madness into the minds of others; its users need not be mad themselves.

title: Dominate
summary: Commanding and rewriting minds through eye contact.

claims.text: Dominate bends another's thoughts and actions by force of will, and needs eye contact.

title: Fortitude
summary: Supernatural toughness, even against fire and sunlight.

claims.text: Fortitude gives a toughness beyond the already sturdy undead body.

title: Necromancy
summary: Power over the dead and the souls of the dead, practised by the Giovanni.

claims.text: Necromancy commands the souls of the dead and, like Thaumaturgy, works through paths and rituals.

title: Obfuscate
summary: Hiding from notice and wearing false faces.

claims.text: An Obfuscated vampire is not invisible but clouds the minds of watchers so they do not notice.

title: Obtenebration
summary: The Lasombra mastery of living shadow.

claims.text: Obtenebration, the Lasombra's signature, grants power over darkness itself.

title: Potence
summary: Supernatural strength.

claims.text: Potence grants strength for great leaps, lifting and brutal blows.

title: Presence
summary: Supernatural charisma, awe and dread.

claims.text: Presence manipulates emotions, stirring fervour or terror in mortals and Kindred.

title: Protean
summary: Changing shape, from claws to wolf to mist.

claims.text: Protean lets a vampire change shape.

title: Quietus
summary: The Assamite art of silent killing and poisonous blood.

claims.text: Quietus, the Assamite art of silent death, works through blood, poison and pestilence.

title: Serpentis
summary: The Setite gifts of the serpent.

claims.text: Serpentis is held to be the legacy of Set, taught only to those the Setites judge worthy.

title: Thaumaturgy
summary: Blood magic of paths and rituals, kept by the Tremere.

claims.text: Thaumaturgy splits into paths, used at will, and rituals, more like formal spells.

title: Vicissitude
summary: The Tzimisce art of shaping flesh and bone.

claims.text: Vicissitude, the Tzimisce's signature, shapes flesh and bone and is rarely taught outside the Clan.

title: Lupines
summary: Kindred name for the werewolves, deadly foes who hold the wild lands beyond the cities.

claims.text: Packs of savage Lupines roam outside the cities, one reason vampires stay in them.

title: The Fae, Seen by the Kindred
summary: To vampires, faeries are capricious legends with no interest in their affairs, until they take one.

claims.text: Faeries seem to belong to two courts and care nothing for vampires, so any meeting depends on their whims.
A faerie's interest can bring a vampire cruel jokes or deadly feuds.

title: Ghosts and the Veil
summary: The restless dead beyond the Veil, whom only a few Kindred understand.

claims.text: A Veil separates the living from the dead, and some ghosts linger on this side of it.
The Giovanni, some Tremere and members of the True Black Hand know something of the dead.
Kindred scholars believe the ghosts have an empire of their own in the Underworld.
